newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil touches 3-1/2-yr low, meal ends lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil touches 3-1/2-yr low, meal ends lower.

text.p: Heavy losses in CBOT soybeans helped push CBOT July soyoil futures to a 3-1/2-year low Thursday, and soymeal futures also ended lower.
Large supplies of soyoil and weak demand for U.S. product in export markets caused all months to score fresh contract lows again Thursday, traders said.
USDA on Thursday reported U.S. net export sales of soyoil for the week ended June 19 were 30,100 tonnes.
That figure was above expectations for 1,000 to 3,000 tonnes, but some U.S. exporters characterized a 28,400-tonne sale to China in the report as a "special deal."
Further sales of U.S. soyoil to China are unlikely because U.S. soyoil prices are still at a premium to other edible oil markets, traders said.

Soymeal futures were also under pressure from weakness in world soymeal basis levels, traders said. Soymeal basis in Brazil on Wednesday fell to $42.00 per ton under July futures from $29.00 under July on Tuesday.
July soyoil closed down 0.10 cent a lb at 22.36, and other months were 0.05 to 0.14 lower. July soymeal closed down $5.00 per ton at 263.90, and other months were down $2.00 to $4.10.
The weakness in soymeal basis sparked widespread concerns that China would default on recent purchases of Brazilian soymeal, traders said.
In soymeal trade, ADM bought 500 lots July and 100 August, Continental bought 1,100 lots August and Cargill bought 500 lots July. Merrill Lynch sold 400 lots July, traders said.
In soyoil trade on the day, FIMAT Futures sold 400 lots July and Dean Witter sold 600 lots August. Griffin Trading bought 500 lots July, pit sources said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 23,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 21,761 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 35,000 lots, against Wednesday's 32,924.
